; Advance the four-channel audio engine once per frame; the fixed interrupt banks this engine in before calling.
; A selects a song/effect or one of the FC..FF control commands. The busy flag prevents the frame update from seeing a partially installed stream.
; Look up the command's word pointer and compare its priority nibble against the current stream. Lower-priority requests return without replacing it.

; Install the primary stream and initialize four channel records, each 31 bytes at AudioChannels. Two stream bytes seed each record; the remaining working bytes are cleared. The channel mask selects which records are active.
; Merge the other priority nibble, load a secondary stream and mask, and initialize only the selected channels. Primary/secondary masks decide which stream supplies each hardware channel.
; Store a command parameter in the tempo/fade controls; the second entry starts its accumulator and retains only the phase bit.
; Clear the high priority nibble and walk the primary channel mask. The complete four-channel control flow is now classified; natural use of every command remains unproven.
; Initialize one selected channel, then advance the packed channel source by four bytes. The enclosing loop uses the saved channel count.
; Advance the four-byte source entry and clear the command latch after all requested channels are initialized.
; A channel with an existing cursor invalidates its modulation cache; an empty channel consumes the selected command header. Restore its preset in either case.
; Clear the low priority nibble and tempo controls, then begin resetting the per-channel stream records. The complete channel reset continuation is included below.
; Finish clearing a channel cursor, restore its APU state, and repeat for the remaining requested channels.
; Clear 15 working bytes after the channel's 16-byte prefix. X advances through the selected channel record; the command/header bytes stay intact.
; Preserve the command pointer while selecting a four-byte modulation preset from the low five preset bits. Copy it to the channel record and restore the command pointer.
; Rotate the channel activity mask and advance the record offset by 31 bytes. The second entry discards four mask bits after a pass.

; Silence the current hardware channel: ordinary channels receive control 30; triangle receives zero in control and both period/length registers. X identifies the APU quartet and is advanced by three only on the triangle path.
; Disable sweep, enable the four tonal/noise channels and advance the audio phase. Return immediately while a command is changing stream state.
; Visit four 31-byte channel records. Update secondary and primary streams as selected by the masks, silence inactive hardware channels, and advance record/APU offsets together.
; At the selected phase, advance the fade accumulator up to 15 and stop or repeat according to the signed mode byte. The audible interpretation of each mode is tentative.
; Count down the shared stream delay and discard the low four channel-mask bits before returning.
; Extract the channel's low-nibble level (triangle uses its full value), then adjust it with the shared fade accumulator. Results remain bounded by the current level.
; Advance the channel's signed envelope step at its configured interval, clamp its low nibble and combine it with hardware control bits. APU quartet offset follows the current channel.

; Update the level modulation accumulator with endpoint reversal, limit output to the computed level, and write the channel control register. Triangle and masked secondary channels take separate paths.
; Add a signed pitch step into the channel's 16-bit pitch accumulator. Secondary-mask state can end the update before the remaining modulation work.
; At each interval add or subtract the encoded pitch delta; reverse phase after the configured span. Bit 7 holds direction/continuation state rather than part of the magnitude.

; Combine the base period and modulation, special-case the noise channel's nibble/mode, and write the APU period registers. Cache the high period so length is retriggered only when it changes. The trailing entry silences the current channel.
; Unknown physical 50466..50468; bank6 CPU $8512..$8514.
; Bytes A9 07 could encode an isolated immediate load, but no independent entry contract or data structure distinguishes the roles.
; The preceding JMP cannot fall through; the next established routine overwrites A. See audio-residual-review.json.
; Reset pitch phase and six modulation counters; optionally seed the level accumulator from the current command field. Mark the cached period high byte invalid to force the next write.
; Reset the modulation state while preserving the cached high period byte, avoiding an unwanted hardware retrigger.

; Pop the caller's return address and use X to select an inline word target. The jump consumes the dispatch table instead of returning through its bytes. Unclassified targets/table bytes remain unresolved.
; Honor the shared stream delay, then process a secondary channel's held period/level. A null period returns immediately.

; Fetch secondary stream commands. High-bit commands either dispatch a special operation or load a period; lower commands use the inline handler table. The seven-word inline handler domain is classified; natural selection of every command remains unresolved.
; Seven secondary-command inline target words consumed by8554. Individual game meanings remain unresolved.
; Read a shared delay from the secondary stream and resume command decoding.
; Read the next secondary byte into record offset 16 and continue decoding; its exact musical meaning is unresolved.
; Merge streamed bitfields into record offset 19. The two entries preserve opposite control-bit groups, with a triangle exception.
; Use the streamed repeat count and a 16-bit destination to loop the secondary stream; when the count is exhausted skip the encoded destination and clear the counter.
; Load four consecutive streamed parameters into channel offsets 20..23, then resume command decoding.
; Back up the secondary cursor, clear priority/activity and choose the surviving primary channel state. Restore modulation from the selected preset before continuing.
; Return to the stream interpreter after the secondary command handler finishes.
; Read one byte from the 16-bit secondary cursor, advance it with carry and return the byte in both A and X.
; Check the tempo control before stepping a primary channel. A static alternate path preserves A around a channel update; the alternate channel path is now included in the current source.
; Finish the bounded parameter-copy loop; the byte count is carried on the stack.
; Optionally take a second tick on alternate phases, subtract four from the 16-bit duration and keep the current note while time remains. A surviving period updates its output each tick.
; At duration expiry clear the continuation bit and decode a new primary command. High nibbles select note/control classes; note durations come from encoded duration tables.
; Resolve a note through the selected period table, store its period and reset its envelope if enabled. Secondary ownership can defer the hardware update.
; Move the command's low bits into the channel's high note-control bits while retaining the preset index.

; Set the continuation flag and keep decoding; the alternate inline-dispatch entry selects special primary commands. The ten-word inline table and its handlers are classified; exact musical command names remain tentative.
; Ten primary-command inline target words consumed by8554. Individual game meanings remain unresolved.
; Read a primary stream byte into record offset 4, used by the duration multiplication routine.
; Consume one command byte as channel pitch step, then resume primary stream parsing.
; Merge primary stream control bitfields into channel offset 12, preserving the other bit group and respecting triangle handling.

; Compare the repeat counter against the streamed limit, update it while preserving the continuation flag, and replace the channel cursor with a streamed word. The exhausted-loop skip path is only partially classified.
; Advance the primary stream cursor by two with carry into its high byte, then resume parsing. This is a cursor operation, not a claim about the original command name.
; Index a word table in the audio bank and store its address in channel offsets 7..8 for subsequent note lookup.
; Decode a duration class through a second table and return to the shared duration/note path.
; Read envelope interval and packed signed-step/level bytes, reset the envelope counter and initialize its level endpoint.
; Seed the envelope's low level nibble to zero or fifteen according to the sign of its configured direction, preserving the packed high nibble.
; Merge a preset index into the channel control byte. If the channel owns hardware output, install the corresponding four-byte modulation preset.
; Compute preset_base + 4*X and copy four bytes to channel offsets 20..23. The helper advances the source pointer across page boundaries.
; Clear the primary cursor and low priority nibble. If the channel mask requests restoration, reinitialize the selected hardware channel through the common audio helper.
; Read through the cursor at channel offsets 0..1, advance that cursor with carry and return the byte in A and X.

; Multiply A by the channel's duration scale through repeated addition, keeping the 16-bit result in offsets 2..3. A zero scale would wrap the eight-bit loop; valid stream constraints remain unresolved.

; Audio duration-class bytes followed by period-word lookup data. The command interpreter uses these to scale duration and select 16-bit periods. Independent boundaries end at the command-header pointer table; exact note names, tuning model and original generator are unresolved.

; Return without updating this actor. The handler selector/caller contract determines when this no-op is used.
; Search slots fifteen down to one. Return Y and carry clear for a free state slot; carry set means every non-player slot is active.

; Reject an invisible source, save its Y and 16-bit world X, and scan other visible actors. The source collision profile selects vertical/horizontal extents; carry clear reports overlap and changes the source animation.

; Most target handlers receive a hit marker; handlers $08/$09/$25 are exceptions. Select contact animation $2A or $2B without replacing animation $1B.

; Two 32-byte actor contact extents: vertical at $814A and horizontal at $816A in mapper bank six. The source actor collision profile, masked to seven bits, selects the tolerated absolute position separation; callers establish the supported profile domain.
; A selects paired 16-bit vertical velocity and horizontal magnitude tables. Caller supplies a supported preset index; these two table domains are not interchangeable with actor selectors.

; Two 32-word motion-preset tables in mapper bank six: vertical velocity at $81A5 and horizontal speed at $81E5. SetMotionPreset doubles A for word indexing; individual handlers may normalize signs or interpret the words as signed increments.
; Visible actors with a nonzero hit marker switch animation and enter the shared reaction path; offscreen actors use that same reaction path. The actor species is unresolved.
; Initialize vertical velocity and horizontal speed once, choose facing relative to the player and select one of two vertical collision paths from state bit one.
; At the vertical apex, clear velocity and return to the falling state. The shared continuation handles horizontal travel and the next grounded jump.
; Step falling motion against terrain, reset animation on a clear probe result, then move horizontally according to facing. A grounded stationary actor advances its state.
; Reset fractional vertical speed and launch with integer speed four.
